releases.title: v1.64.0
releases.highlights: 🧰 WebMCP New page.webmcp and frame.webmcp give access to the tools that a page registers through the experimental WebMCP browser API, so you can test them like any other part of your app: browser = chromium . launch ( args = [ "--enable-features=WebMCP" ]) page = browser . new_page () page . goto ( "https://example.com" ) for tool in page . webmcp . tools (): print ( tool [ "name" ], tool [ "description" ]) result = page . webmcp . call_tool ( "add" , { "a" : 2 , "b" : 40 }) print ( result [ "content" ][ 0 ][ "text" ]) # "42" Playwright MCP also supports WebMCP by default, with page-defined tools offered to the agent as webmcp_<tool> . Pass --no-webmcp to opt out. playwright-cli exposes them as well: playwright-cli webmcp-list playwright-cli webmcp-call search_catalog --params ' {"query":"cats"} ' 🎬 Better videos Videos can now be recorded at a custom frame rate, and the decorations for actions are styled with plain CSS: page . screencast . start ( path = "video.webm" , size = { "width" : 1920 , "height" : 1080 }, fps = 60 ) page . screencast . show_actions ( style = { "point" : "width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 50%; background: red" , "highlight" : "outline: 2px solid #3…

releases.title: v1.63.0
releases.highlights: 🪟 Locate across frames page.frame_locator() and frame.frame_locator() called without a selector search in any frame of the subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first: # Finds the button in any frame on the page. page . frame_locator (). get_by_role ( "button" ). click () The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it matches elements in several frames. 👁️ Visible-only locators New locator.visible returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended replacement for the :visible CSS pseudo-class: page . locator ( "button" ). visible . click () 🖼️ Aria and screen snapshots in traces New aria_snapshots and screen_snapshots options of tracing.start() capture an aria snapshot and a screenshot of the page on every action: context . tracing . start ( snapshots = True , aria_snapshots = True , screen_snapshots = True ) With aria and screen snapshots recorded, the new Display Aria mode in the trace viewer shows the action screenshot side by side with the aria snapshot, and hovering an aria node highlights it on the screenshot. releases.title: v1.62.0
releases.highlights: 🖼️ WebP screenshots page.screenshot() and locator.screenshot() can now capture screenshots in the WebP format. Playwright infers the format from a .webp file extension, or you can set the type explicitly. Quality 100 (the default) is lossless, while lower values use lossy compression: page . screenshot ( path = "homepage.webp" , quality = 50 ) New APIs New scroll option ( "auto" | "none" ) on actions to opt out of Playwright's automatic scrolling into view. New locator.wait_for_function() waits until a function called with the matching element returns a truthy value. New apiResponse.timing() returns resource timing information for an API response. Announcements 📋 The clipboard is now isolated from the operating system in headless mode, so tests that use navigator.clipboard no longer read or overwrite the clipboard of the machine running them. ⚠️ Debian 11 is not supported anymore. Browser Versions Chromium 151.0.7922.34 Mozilla Firefox 153.0 WebKit 26.5 This version was also tested against the following stable channels: Google Chrome 151 Microsoft Edge 151

releases.title: v1.61.0
releases.highlights: 🔑 WebAuthn passkeys New Credentials virtual authenticator, available via browserContext.credentials , lets tests register passkeys and answer navigator.credentials.create() / navigator.credentials.get() ceremonies in the page — no real hardware key required, works in all browsers: context = browser . new_context () # Seed a passkey your backend provisioned for a test user. context . credentials . create ( "example.com" , id = credential_id , user_handle = user_handle , private_key = private_key , public_key = public_key , ) context . credentials . install () page = context . new_page () page . goto ( "https://example.com/login" ) # The page's navigator.credentials.get() is answered with the seeded passkey. You can also let the app register a passkey once in a setup test, read it back with credentials.get() , and seed it into later tests — see Credentials for details. 🗃️ Web Storage New WebStorage API, available via page.localStorage and page.sessionStorage , reads and writes the page's storage for the current origin: page . local_storage . set_item ( "token" , "abc" ) token = page . local_storage . get_item ( "token" ) items = page . session_storage . items () New APIs apiResponse…

releases.title: v1.60.0
releases.highlights: 🐍 Python improvements New FormData class for building multipart/form-data request bodies — pass to api_request_context.post(form=…) etc. expect.soft(...) soft assertions collect multiple failures in a test instead of stopping at the first one. Requires up-to-date pytest integration to work. All timeout parameters now accept datetime.timedelta — applies wherever a timeout is taken, e.g. page.goto() , locator.click() , expect(...).to_be_visible() . Async context manager support across more APIs — async with now works for objects returned from screencast.show_actions() , screencast.show_overlays() , etc. page.expect_request(...) and page.expect_response(...) now accept async predicates. Typed overloads for expect_event / wait_for_event so the event payload type is inferred per event name. 🌐 HAR recording on Tracing tracing.start_har() / tracing.stop_har() expose HAR recording as a first-class tracing API, with the same content , mode and url_filter options as record_har : context . tracing . start_har ( "trace.har" ) page = context . new_page () page . goto ( "https://playwright.dev" ) context . tracing . stop_har () 🪝 Drop API New locator.drop() simulates an external drag-and-drop o…

releases.title: 0.13.13: OpenAI browser tools and Cloud fixes
releases.highlights: This release includes the OpenAI browser-tool driver and fixes two integration issues. Handle temporary empty Cloud tab URLs during navigation. Keep screenshots, crops, and pointer coordinates aligned on scaled displays. Provide 18 default browser tools and six optional actions through Browser Use Actor. Support local browsers, Browser Use Cloud, and borrowed browser sessions. Install the openai-tools extra with OpenAI Python 3.31+. OpenAI 3.x uses httpx2; use its DefaultAsyncHttpxClient for custom HTTP clients. Validation: all eleven driver tests pass. Both new regression tests fail on the earlier implementation. Pre-commit, type checks, package builds, and GitHub tests pass. Live remote-browser and library smoke tests passed; broader evaluation results remain separate. This release supersedes 0.13.12, whose PyPI publication was cancelled before approval. Guide: https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/customize/integrations/openai Driver: #6086 Fixes: #6089

releases.title: 0.13.12: OpenAI browser tools
releases.highlights: Add OpenAI browser tools backed by Browser Use Actor. Import BrowserUse from browser_use.integrations.openai . Install browser-use[openai-tools] to enable OpenAI Python 3.31+. Use local browsers, Browser Use Cloud, or an existing connected BrowserSession. Support the 18 default browser tools and six optional actions. Preserve borrowed browser ownership and check Cloud browser cleanup. Preserve URL and timeout settings across OpenAI 2.x and 3.x model wrappers. OpenAI 3.x uses httpx2. For custom HTTP clients, use OpenAI's DefaultAsyncHttpxClient. This integration does not yet provide uploads, downloads, scoped reads, console/network diagnostics, or Bash. Validation: 35 integration/model tests passed, two skipped; OpenAI 2.26 compatibility: 15 passed, one skipped. All pull-request checks passed. Live Cloud navigation and element-reference click tests passed with provider-confirmed cleanup. Implementation: #6086 Cloud tests: https://github.com/browser-use/new-eval-platform/actions/runs/38824343560

This release includes Browser Use toolsets for Claude, available at browser_use.integrations.toolsets_for_claude . The integration requires an Anthropic SDK release containing anthropic.tools.browser ; the current public Anthropic SDK does not yet include it. Documentation: https://docs.browser-use.com/open-source/customize/integrations/toolsets-for-claude PyPI publication runs through the protected release workflow and requires a separate reviewer approval. Defaults for omitted Query , Header , Cookie , and Form parameters and model fields are no longer treated as user input. Defaults are not validated unless validate_default=True is enabled. If you rely on validators running for omitted values, enable default validation with Field(validate_default=True) for model fields or, for example, Query(validate_default=True) for individual parameters. Body(validate_default=True) is now honored too. For parameter models, applying a default no longer marks a field as explicitly set, so model_dump(exclude_unset=True) excludes it. Default factories run once, and validation errors no longer include injected defaults in input . Omitted boolean form fields still become False and count as explicitly set. Breaking Changes 🐛 Fix default handling for request parameters and models. PR #16527 by @tiangolo .

Omitted bool and bool | None form fields are now interpreted as False , matching unchecked HTML checkboxes. This applies to individual Form parameters and form models, including required fields and fields with defaults of True or None . The inferred value is considered explicitly set, including in model_dump(exclude_unset=True) . JSON requests and direct Pydantic validation are unchanged. See Boolean Form Fields . Breaking Changes 🐛 Treat omitted boolean form fields as False. PR #16523 by @tiangolo . Internal ✅ Add tests for parameter defaults, nullability, and browser form behavior. PR #14829 by @YuriiMotov .

The root_path parameter in FastAPI() is deprecated. Configure the server with fastapi run --root-path /api/v1 instead. Breaking Changes 🗑️ Deprecate the root_path parameter in FastAPI . PR #16520 by @tiangolo .
Breaking Changes 🔥 Remove deprecated openapi_prefix and unused **extra from FastAPI . PR #16518 by @tiangolo . Docs 📝 Document URL paths in templates. PR #16517 by @tiangolo .
Features ✨ Add WebSocket support to security dependencies. PR #10147 by @mnixry .
